thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident 2765432109 created — partial region flip failure: eu -> na. Pager routed to oncall.

alex: seeing a surge of 502s for eu-edge during the flip. Canary health checks started failing around t+2m. Not sure if it's app or routing.

marta: confirming, Grafana shows error-rate spike from 0.3% -> 12% for eu-prod-inference between 2765432110 and 2765432140. Latency also up.

samira: oncall ENG-SRE here. Paging in — what's the rollout command that executed?

alex: release pipeline moved weight: eu 10% -> 70% -> 100%. We ran the automated geo-weight flip. Logs: `deploy/rollout 2765432109 --from eu --to na --mode gradual --steps 10m`

lia: DNS team — any outstanding changes? We lowered edge DNS TTL to 30s before flip. No DNS pushes in last 10 mins.

dns-ops: we did NOT push new records. However, our monitoring shows a handful of eu resolver nodes still returning old A records pointing at green pool IPs that are half behind a drain. Likely stale caches.

samira: so partial traffic hitting drained hosts + new hosts behind different health checks -> 502s. Can we stop the flip and force rollback?

eng-release-bot: Rollout automation reports: step 6/10 completed, target weight 70%. Continue halted due to health-check threshold breach.

alex: health-check failures look like 503/502 from proxy -> backend not responding to new token handshake (tls_sni mismatch) — suspicious. Could be envoy config mismatch between blue/green.

marta: customer impact assessment: ~8% of requests from EU customers experienced errors during ramp. Top customers by volume: two mid-market SaaS customers saw elevated error rates. No P0 yet.

support-oncall: pinged CS with initial note: "We see intermittent 502s for EU users during regional rollout — possible rollback in progress." They've queued customers that reported issues.

samira: immediate actions: 1) Kill-switch feature flag for geo-flip 2) Freeze rollout 3) Route traffic back to stable pool 4) Open a rollback if required. Who can flip the flag fast?

marta: I can flip the feature flag. Flag path: `flags.geo_edge_flip` environment: prod.

alex: also recommend setting route weight eu -> stable 100% now. Command: ```sh
rctl geo set-weight eu stable 100
rctl geo set-weight eu new 0
```

lia: DNS workaround: increase TTL bounce? nah, better to avoid more DNS churn. We'll keep TTL low and coordinate route weights.

samira: doing flag kill-switch now.

marta: I toggled `flags.geo_edge_flip` -> off at 2765432165. Confirmed via admin UI.

eng-release-bot: Automated pipeline detected flag off — halting automated steps. Current partial weight frozen at 70%.

alex: executing route commands to set eu back to stable. Running: `rctl geo set-weight eu stable 100`

alex: done at 2765432190. Weight set confirmed by routing-api.

dns-ops: observing slow decrease in errors — likely because new hosts are draining and stable pool now serving majority. Some resolver caches still point to drained IPs for another ~30s.

marta: telemetry: error-rate dropping from 12% -> 1.5% over last 90s. Latency normalizing. Still monitoring top customers.

support-oncall: CS updated: "We've stopped the rollout and routed EU traffic back to stable — monitoring. Will escalate if errors persist."

samira: next steps: 1) Run a controlled canary on a small subset with additional telemetry checks (auth handshake validation), 2) Validate envoy config parity between pools, 3) Confirm DNS resolver health across regions, 4) Postmortem. Owner: samira + alex.

marta: creating a short incident ticket and marking customer-impacted list. I'll coordinate postmortem notes.

alex: quick debug note — found a config diff: sni_hostname set to `edge.internal` on green, but `edge-v2.internal` on blue-backends. That explains handshake mismatch when new traffic hit some backends.

samira: good catch. Do we have automated config parity checks?

alex: we have a lint but it missed this. Adding a check to the rollout gate.

lia: DNS ops will run a sweep across resolvers to make sure none are persistently caching weird records.

dns-ops: sweep started at 2765432300. Found 3 EU resolvers with stale cache; we've triggered a push and they'll clear within TTL.

samira: handoff: I'm going to coordinate the rollback validation and run the small canary at 2765432500. On-call rotation: alex will stay for immediate followups; marta will own customer comms; lia/dns-ops will monitor DNS.

incident-bot: Incident 2765432109 status: mitigated (service restored to stable pool). Postmortem draft assigned to samira.

marta: tagging for postmortem: cause=config-drift, impact=partial-eu-traffic-error, mitigation=flag-kill-switch+route-set, action-items=[config parity check in pipeline, canary telemetry gate, dns resolver sweep].

support-oncall: closing the CS loop for now — will reopen per CS if customers escalate.

samira: thanks all. Will publish a short RCA within 48h. Please add any loose threads here.

alex: also adding note to release runbook: prefer staged canary with config parity verification step before >25% weight.

marta: thanks, team :thumbsup:
